remaining_references.text: For MDEA, which tests the shared inorganic-carbon description without an amine-carbamate pathway, substituting Part I's bound bicarbonate--water interaction and R2 law moves the unfitted error in the direction opposite to AMP before refitting, and the MDEA cation--bicarbonate interaction reaches its bound; this pattern does not identify a uniquely defective bicarbonate parameter.
The compiled \texttt{epcsaft} library evaluates the equation of state and its equilibrium derivatives; Supplementary Section~S8 records the immutable file identity used in the calculations.

The monoethanolamine (MEA) fit in Part I supplies the frozen water, carbon dioxide and inorganic-ion parameters for the present electrolyte perturbed-chain statistical associating fluid theory (ePC-SAFT) calculations \cite{PolleyPartI}.
Here the water, \COtwo and inorganic-ion parameters from Part I remain fixed while only amine-specific quantities are fitted.
Part I's bicarbonate--water interaction lies on its upper bound, so MDEA tests the shared inorganic-carbon description without an amine-carbamate pathway \cite{PolleyPartI}.
The selected parameters remain fixed for the reported comparisons; the start and bound inventory records the alternatives (Supplementary Section~S3).
Unlike the penalized MEA fit of Part I \cite[Sect.~4.5]{PolleyPartI}, the reported MDEA, AMP, PZ and DEA fits contain no stability penalty; their phases were searched after fitting.

The water and \COtwo component descriptions, hydronium, hydroxide, bicarbonate and carbonate, all interactions among these six shared species, and the reaction laws of Part I, R1 (water autoprotolysis), R2 (\ce{CO2 + 2H2O <=> HCO3- + H3O+}) and R3 (\ce{HCO3- + H2O <=> CO3^{2-} + H3O+}), including Part I's fitted R2 corrections, are held fixed \cite{PolleyPartI}.

The MDEA and AMP fits were first developed against an earlier MEA fit whose bicarbonate--water interaction was 0.727 rather than Part I's bound value $+1$ and whose R2 coefficients differed slightly (Supplementary Section~S7); Section~\ref{sec:p2-shared-sensitivity} tests that difference.
Water retains the exponential temperature dependence tabulated by Pabsch et al. \cite[Table~2]{Pabsch2020}, with its constant term fitted to IAPWS-95 in Part I \cite{PolleyPartI}:

MDEA, AMP and DEA coefficients use Hsieh et al.'s unloaded measurements at model liquid densities \cite[Tables~1--2, 4--5, 7]{hsiehDielectricConstantsAqueous2007}; PZ and HPZCOO use the MEA coefficients fitted in Part I as an assumption \cite{PolleyPartI}.
The separately fitted PZ--water binary properties retain discrepancies that the reactive refit leaves unchanged (Supplementary Sections~S1 and S3).
For Carson heat, scaled RMS increases from 0.977 with the earlier shared description to 1.106 after refitting to the Part I shared description.
Only that block lies inside both PZ laws; the 395.0 K rows also exceed the shared R2 interval (Supplementary Table~\ref{supp-tab:p2-kamps-blocks}).
Lal's low-pressure observations, which the source reports as less accurate, remain in the AARD (Supplementary Section~S4).
Forty-three comparison-only loaded DEA densities at 298.15 K give 0.445\,\% AARD (Supplementary Section~S4); the fitted MDEA density groups are given in Table~\ref{tab:p2-calibration}.
AMP's carbamate diameter and enthalpy correction reach limits with nearly flat inward profiles (Supplementary Section S6).

Unfitted pressures depend on the shared description as well as on the amine fit: substituting Part I's bicarbonate--water interaction and R2 law moves the MDEA and AMP errors by 22--26 percentage points in opposite directions before the amine parameters are refitted (Table~\ref{tab:p2-shared-sensitivity}).

Table~\ref{tab:p2-shared-sensitivity} follows the same data through the earlier shared description, substitution of the Part I bicarbonate--water interaction and fitted R2 law, and amine-specific refitting.

Small property residuals do not exclude false liquid phases: the reported PZ fit has at least forty across calibration and comparison states, and a separate fit with the Part I stability penalty still has at least three, two of which the standard finite search missed.

This counterexample demonstrates a missed finite search, so every split count in this paper is a lower bound, and the absence of detected instability, here and for the penalized MEA fit of Part I \cite[Sect.~4.5]{PolleyPartI}, does not prove stability.
Only the constant term in that law was fitted in Part I; the exponential coefficients were fixed.
The MEA joint-fit R2 coefficients retain their conditional uncertainty in Part I, but no uncertainty of those shared inputs is propagated here.

The separate penalty fit uses the Part I tangent-plane requirement at 245 states: the 121 NMR liquids and each Hilliard feed as an all-liquid parent at 1.05 and three times its candidate bubble pressure.

Consequently detected-split counts are lower bounds in both Part I and this paper, and a count of states without detected instability is an upper bound on stability within the searched inventory, not proof of global stability.
Substituting Part I's shared bicarbonate--water interaction and R2 without refitting gives 21.89\,\% and $-15.10$\,\%, while worsening the fitted total pressures.
The earlier bicarbonate--water interaction is 0.72705584775, compared with one in Part I.
